base_requirements: Canvas slice mandate: adapt the Laravel package declaration surface to v1 response-time-budget, domain-expiry, API assertion-metadata, secret-masking, sync-summary, documentation, facade, and backward-compatibility requirements without implementing monitor runtime behavior
PRD 4.2: website declarations support domain-expiry warning at 30 days and a p95 response-time budget whose v1 warning threshold defaults to 2000 milliseconds
PRD 4.3: API declarations support custom headers plus ordered status, latency, and JSON response-shape assertions

PRD 4.3 security: package-held header and token plaintext may cross the authenticated HTTPS sync request but must be masked from command output, exceptions, logs, debug output, documentation examples, and integration evidence; encryption at rest remains downstream runtime ownership

Inherited CheckSyncPayloadContract: registry and config definitions serialize to check-sync.v1 with canonical uptime, ssl, api, dead_links, open_graph, domain_expiry, and response_time_budget arrays and are validated against the foundation-owned generated schema rather than a package-local duplicate
Backward compatibility: existing uptime, SSL, API, link, and OpenGraph fluent methods, config sections, options, precedence, and legacy sync-summary aliases continue to work

Canvas owned sdk-to-check-sync-contract seam and integration requirement: package serialization is proven through a real sync HTTP request, the foundation harness event API, registered outbox relay, real queue worker, and receipt API in the canonical full-runtime Playwright harness

path.project_id: opaque non-empty project identifier from checkybot-laravel.project_id; URL-encoded by the client and never accepted from an individual check definition

body.uptime: array of {name, url, interval, max_redirects?, headers?}
body.api: array of {name, url, interval, headers?, expected_status?, max_latency_ms?, retry_count?, assertions?}; assertions are ordered metadata for status, latency, or JSON response-shape evaluation
body.dead_links: array of {name, url, interval, max_depth?, exclude_paths?, headers?}
body.open_graph: array of {name, url, interval, required_tags?, headers?}
body.domain_expiry: array of {name, url, interval, warn_days}; v1 default warn_days is 30
body.response_time_budget: array of {name, url, interval, percentile, budget_ms}; v1 defaults are percentile 95 and budget_ms 2000

request.validation: Every array is required, including empty arrays. Names are non-empty and unique within a type, URLs pass FILTER_VALIDATE_URL and use http or https, intervals match /^\d+[smhd]$/, thresholds and existing type options are bounded, and API assertion kind/operator/operand/path combinations are valid. Invalid local definitions stop before HTTP; downstream contract validation returns 422.
request.authorization: The bearer key must be authorized to manage the route project. Production transport must be HTTPS; only the canonical loopback harness may use HTTP. Header/token values remain unmasked only inside the in-memory outbound body so the downstream service can encrypt them at rest.

200.summary: object containing created, updated, and deleted non-negative integer counts for canonical uptime|ssl|api|dead_links|open_graph|domain_expiry|response_time_budget keys or the compatible legacy *_checks/link_checks aliases

403.message: The API key cannot manage this project.

422.errors: object keyed by invalid payload field

response.transport_failure: CheckybotSyncException with bounded redacted text and no API key, header value, bearer token, cookie value, or payload secret

request.availability: canonical testing runtime only; loopback-bound and absent in production

body.payload: the exact check-sync.v1 body captured from the SDK sync HTTP request, including all seven canonical arrays

request.validation: The payload must pass the foundation-owned CheckSyncPayloadContract; malformed fields and unknown contract versions return 422 before enqueueing.
request.authorization: Harness-only loopback access; no production registration.

request.availability: canonical testing runtime only; loopback-bound and absent in production

backend_milestone_items.title: V1 fluent and config monitor definition contracts
backend_milestone_items.contract_excerpt: Within inherited ownership, add focused domain-expiry and response-time-budget check builders, registry arrays/factories/getters/count/flush support, matching config and publishable-stub sections, and one check-sync.v1 serializer shared by fluent and config paths. Emit exactly the foundation-owned canonical arrays: uptime, ssl, api, dead_links, open_graph, domain_expiry, and response_time_budget. Add API status, latency, and ordered JSON response-shape assertion metadata while retaining the current fluent assertion vocabulary. ConfigValidator remains the local boundary and uses FILTER_VALIDATE_URL plus /^\d+[smhd]$/. Sensitive header/token values are held only as needed to build the outbound request; safe/debug/console representations mask values, and this package does not claim encryption-at-rest or evaluator behavior.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit and config tests prove domain-expiry and response-time-budget definitions can be declared through both fluent factories and config, serialize identically into their canonical check-sync.v1 arrays, default to warn_days=30 and percentile=95/budget_ms=2000, and preserve valid explicit thresholds.

API-check unit tests prove fluent status, maximum-latency, and chained JSON response-shape assertions serialize as deterministic ordered metadata with stable sort_order and is_active values and preserve scalar operand types required by the generated contract.

A fixed secret-corpus test proves Authorization, bearer-token, cookie, and custom-header plaintext appears only in the captured outbound HTTPS request body and never in dry-run or summary output, exception text, Laravel logs, object debug output, safe serialization, snapshots, or integration evidence.

Table-driven ConfigValidator tests prove fluent and config definitions reject duplicate names per type, URLs failing FILTER_VALIDATE_URL or non-http(s) schemes, intervals outside /^\d+[smhd]$/, out-of-range domain/budget/status/latency/retry values, and invalid assertion kind/operator/path/operand combinations before any HTTP request is made.

Backward-compatibility tests prove existing uptime, ssl, api, links, and openGraph facade methods, interval helpers, existing options and assertion aliases, registry precedence over config, count/flush/getters, and legacy config section names continue to produce the same per-check values inside the canonical versioned payload.

backend_milestone_items.title: Secure sync transport, summaries, documentation, and runtime seam
backend_milestone_items.contract_excerpt: Update CheckybotClient and checkybot:sync to send the versioned canonical payload to the existing project sync route, reject unsafe production base URLs, retain bounded retry/error behavior, and normalize both canonical and legacy summary key profiles for all seven types. Dry-run output lists safe names, URLs, intervals, and type totals without secret-bearing fields. Consume, rather than duplicate or edit, the foundation CheckSyncPayloadContract generated schema. For the owned sdk-to-check-sync-contract seam, add testing-only loopback sync capture/wiring under src that is absent in production, preserve the exact client-emitted body, post it through the real foundation harness event API, execute the registered checkybot:foundation-relay command, and let the canonical real queue worker deliver it before the receipt API is read. The canonical full-runtime Playwright runner may generate run-scoped test code/evidence under build, but reviewable product/test changes remain inside inherited ownership. Update README, CHANGELOG, facade docblocks, config, and stubs with both declaration styles, migration notes, and the explicit security/runtime ownership boundary.

acceptance_criteria.text: CheckybotClient tests prove syncChecks sends one authenticated JSON POST to /api/v1/projects/{encoded_project_id}/checks/sync with contract_version=check-sync.v1 and all seven arrays, accepts declared 200 and harness 202 responses, maps 401/403/422 and transport failures to CheckybotSyncException, and exposes no secret in logs or thrown messages.

Command feature tests prove registry and config syncs count and dry-run-label all seven check types, never print sensitive fields, and render created/updated/deleted totals correctly for both canonical summary keys and legacy uptime_checks|ssl_checks|api_checks|link_checks|open_graph_checks plus new-type *_checks aliases, with absent counts normalized to zero.

Documentation contract tests prove README, CHANGELOG, facade docblocks, published config, and stub contain working fluent and config examples for domain expiry, p95 response budgets, and API status/latency/body assertions; identify check-sync.v1; explain upgrade compatibility; and state that secrets are sent only to the authenticated HTTPS API for downstream encryption and are masked from package output.

Package contract tests validate the exact fluent-generated and config-generated HTTP bodies against the foundation-owned CheckSyncPayloadContract fixtures, accept every current check type and optional field, and reject a missing array, unknown contract version, malformed definition, or package-only unknown top-level key.

The canonical full-runtime Playwright end-to-end test proves the owned sdk-to-check-sync-contract seam by defining all seven types through the real package APIs, capturing the exact body emitted by a real POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/checks/sync, submitting that body as contract.check_sync.probed through POST /__harness/monitor-foundation/events, executing the registered checkybot:foundation-relay command with the real queue worker running, and observing an sdk schema-valid receipt listing all seven types through GET /__harness/monitor-foundation/receipts/{operation_id}, without invoking a validator, processor, job, or consumer directly.
